issues.detail: The identical-ion branch has a source-reported quantitative Kramers-Langer inversion-rate relation, but the isotope-substituted branch supplies only qualitative suppression and a turnstile barrier, not a second source-reported inversion-rate formula.

The identical-ion quantitative rate claim varies with alpha in the pyramidal regime, while the isotope comparison is reported only at alpha approximately 1.09. The source therefore does not provide two quantitative rate branches over one shared controllable alpha query domain.

The identical-ion quantitative response is inversion rate extracted from dwell-time distributions. For the isotope branch, the observed readout is only qualitative locking; its reported numerical quantity is an activation barrier, not an inversion rate. Thus the two branches lack the same source-reported quantitative readout.
